object_description: two-story building with a floating overhanging upper volume
design_condition: The compact building is embedded in the gently rising slope and forest clearing, with its set-back ground floor compensating for terrain changes and the overhanging upper volume creating covered arrival and break areas.

positive.statement: The building fits well into the surroundings despite its large footprint.
The open space concept weaves forest, groups of trees, herbaceous fringe and meadow into the new school building.
The building volume is intelligently placed in the forest clearing and strengthens the spatial conditions through new plantings.
The compact building volume enables different uses to be arranged naturally, well exposed to the sun and accessible by wheelchair.
The ground floor is designed and organized in a very practical and user-oriented manner.
The rooms are well positioned in relation to access, exposure and the outside.
The vertical access at the center promises the shortest possible paths on all sides.
The project impresses with its precision, well-placed building volume, innovative design features and sympathetic materialization.

negative.statement: The windmill-like arrangement produces very winding and narrow corridors on the upper floors, making orientation difficult.
The location of the offices and therapy rooms on the first floor is criticized.
The kindergartens' location on the second floor prevents direct outdoor access.
The open central staircase is not tolerated for fire-safety reasons, and the atriums would require elaborate fire compartments.
The large cubature and graduated atrium incisions require very large and expensive facade processing.
The high proportion of glass has a negative impact on gray energy.
The area and volume efficiency, complex facade construction and expensive courtyards lead to high investment costs.
